titulo: Rules with set dates: what applies now and what's coming
lead: AI regulation feels like a distant topic, but part of it already applies today and part of it has a date on the calendar. Whoever helps companies doesn't need to be a lawyer; you need to know what applies now, what's coming, who it applies to and when to call legal. This lesson organizes all of that into a timeline you build for your own company.
objetivo: build your company's compliance timeline: what applies now, what's coming, who it applies to and who owns each item.

aprende.t: EU AI Act dates after the 2026 postponement
NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001: what they are and what they're for

hero_alt: A paper calendar with days circled in red, thick books stacked up and an hourglass on a dark desk.

secoes.sub: From left to right: what already applies, what has a date and what is voluntary.

nos.detalhe: The LGPD (Brazil's data protection law) already applies to any processing of personal data, including by AI. It is the rule that weighs most today for a Brazilian small or midsize business: legal basis, international transfer, security and the right to review an automated decision (lesson 5).

Under the EU AI Act, the prohibited practices and the AI literacy obligation (art. 4) have applied since 02/02/2025. Whoever provides or uses AI systems must make sure their team understands enough about AI. The rules for general-purpose models and for transparency also stay on the original calendar.

nos.titulo: With a date in the EU
nos.detalhe: The Digital Omnibus package, adopted in July 2026, postponed the high-risk rules: Annex III systems (hiring, credit, education, critical infrastructure) move to 02/12/2027; AI built into regulated products, to 02/08/2028. It applies to a Brazilian company that sells or uses AI in the European market.

itens.t: Special Committee of the Chamber of Deputies

nos.detalhe: PL 2338/2023, which sets rules for the ethical and responsible use of AI, came from the Senate. On the Chamber's record, checked on 10/19/2026, the status is "Awaiting Rapporteur's Opinion in the Special Committee". It is not law yet: keep an eye on it, but don't treat it as an obligation.

The NIST AI RMF (US) is a voluntary guide with four functions: govern, map, measure and manage risks. ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is the AI management system standard, certifiable by an accredited body. Neither is law, but they work as a checklist and a common language with large clients.

secoes.legenda: For each rule, two questions: does it apply to us? Starting when?

secoes.titulo: How to build the company's timeline
secoes.sub: Four steps. Horizonte serves as the example.

texto: Start with the inventory: which tools use AI, what data they process and who the company sells to.
At Horizonte: WhatsApp customer service, conversation summaries, order app, email. Customers only in Brazil.
LGPD: does it process personal data? Almost always yes. EU AI Act: does it sell or use AI in the European Union? At Horizonte, no.
Hiring, credit or education with AI? Flag them: these are high-risk areas under the AI Act and call for extra care in Brazil too.

passos.sub: Already in force, has a date, under discussion
texto: Separate what already applies (act now), what has a date (plan), and what is under discussion (monitor).
Don't treat a bill as law: that spends energy in the wrong place.

passos.titulo: Assign an owner and a next action
texto: Every row needs someone who owns it and a next action, with a date.
Unsure whether a rule applies, about a contract, or about a legal basis? That's when you call legal. You organize; the legal opinion is theirs.

exemplo.texto: LGPD · service summary · owner: Rafael with legal · stop sending without a contract within 30 days.

secoes.sub: One row per rule. Review every quarter.

blocos.rot: Prompt · check whether a rule applies
blocos.conteudo:
Help me organize questions for legal, without giving a legal opinion.
Company: <sector, size, where it sells>
AI use: <what the tool does and what data it handles>
Rule: <LGPD | EU AI Act | PL 2338/2023>

List:
1. Which facts about us decide whether the rule applies.
2. The questions I should take to legal.
Don't say whether the rule applies or not; don't invent articles. If you don't know, say so.

abas.html:
• LGPD · applies (customer data on WhatsApp) · already in force · owner: Carlos with legal · review the service summary in 30 days.
  • EU AI Act · doesn't apply today (no EU customers) · reassess if you export.
  • PL 2338/2023 · under discussion · monitor every quarter.
  • NIST AI RMF · voluntary · use the 4 functions as an internal checklist.

• Treating a bill as law: PL 2338 is still in the Chamber of Deputies.
  • Thinking European law doesn't matter: it matters if the company sells or uses AI in the EU.
  • Giving a legal opinion: you organize facts and questions; legal is the one who concludes.

secoes.sub: Use the inventory from lesson 2. No company? Use Horizonte.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: For Horizonte, which sells only in Brazil, which rule weighs most today?
opcoes: The LGPD, which already applies to personal data handled by AI.
None: AI isn't regulated in Brazil.
perguntas.explica: The LGPD already applies and covers any processing of personal data, including by AI. PL 2338 is still in the Chamber of Deputies. The common mistake is thinking that, without a specific AI law, there are no rules.

perguntas.p: After the Digital Omnibus, when do the AI Act's Annex III high-risk rules start to apply?
perguntas.explica: They were postponed to 02/12/2027, not repealed. Literacy and prohibitions have applied since 02/02/2025. The common mistake is reading "postponed" as "over".

perguntas.p: A question came up about whether a client's use of AI counts as "high risk". What do you do?
opcoes: Answer it yourself, to save time.
Organize the facts and the questions and take them to legal.
Ask the AI and pass its answer along as a legal opinion.
Ignore it until the law changes.
perguntas.explica: You organize; the legal opinion is theirs. That's the limit of your role (lesson 7). The common mistake is passing along an AI answer as if it were a legal opinion.
